title: Coding Challenge 3: Encapsulation
description: Learn the principle of Encapsulation in Object-Oriented Programming. Encapsulation bundles data and methods together while protecting internal state from direct external access. In this challenge, create a SecretDiary class that protects a child's secrets from snooping parents! Use the underscore naming convention (_passcode and _content) for private variables to signify that internal data should not be accessed directly, but only read or written through class methods using the correct passcode.
requirements: The constructor should accept 'owner' and 'passcode' parameters
Use the underscore prefix convention ('this._passcode' and 'this._content') for private variables
Implement a 'write(passcode, text)' method that updates _content and returns 'Entry added' if the passcode is correct, or returns 'Access denied' if incorrect
Implement a 'read(passcode)' method that returns _content if the passcode is correct, or returns 'Access denied' if incorrect
hints: In JavaScript, prefixing variable names with an underscore (like this._passcode and this._content) is the standard convention to indicate private properties
Initialize this.owner = owner, this._passcode = passcode, and this._content = '' inside the constructor
In write() and read(), verify if the incoming passcode parameter matches this._passcode
If the passcode matches, allow reading or updating this._content
Return 'Access denied' when an incorrect passcode is supplied

tests.name: SecretDiary class exists
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('Alice', '1234'); return typeof d === 'object' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'SecretDiary is not a class' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: SecretDiary has public owner property
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('Alice', '1234'); return d.owner === 'Alice' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'owner property is not set correctly' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Uses underscore naming convention for private variables
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('Bob', 'secret123'); const codeStr = SecretDiary.toString(); const hasUnderscore = codeStr.includes('_passcode') || codeStr.includes('_content') || ('_passcode' in d); if (!hasUnderscore) { return { success: false, message: 'Please use the underscore convention (this._passcode and this._content) for private variables' }; } if (d.passcode !== undefined) { return { success: false, message: 'passcode should use underscore prefix (this._passcode)' }; } if (d.content !== undefined) { return { success: false, message: 'content should use underscore prefix (this._content)' }; } return { success: true }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }
tests.successMessage: Underscore convention used for private variables ✓

tests.name: write() updates content with valid passcode
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('Charlie', 'mySecretCode'); const writeRes = d.write('mySecretCode', 'Dear Diary, today was great!'); const readRes = d.read('mySecretCode'); return (writeRes === 'Entry added' && readRes === 'Dear Diary, today was great!') ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'write() or read() failed with valid passcode. Expected write to return "Entry added"' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: read() denies access with incorrect passcode
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('David', 'key999'); d.write('key999', 'Top secret thoughts'); const readRes = d.read('wrongPasscode'); return readRes === 'Access denied' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Expected "Access denied", got "' + readRes + '"' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: write() denies update with incorrect passcode
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('Emma', 'pass123'); d.write('pass123', 'My secret'); const writeRes = d.write('parentSnooping', 'I found your diary!'); const readRes = d.read('pass123'); if (writeRes !== 'Access denied') { return { success: false, message: 'write() should return "Access denied" for incorrect passcode' }; } if (readRes !== 'My secret') { return { success: false, message: 'Diary content should not be changed by unauthorized access' }; } return { success: true }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Encapsulation: methods control access to internal state
tests.test: function() { try { const d1 = new SecretDiary('Fiona', 'codeA'); const d2 = new SecretDiary('George', 'codeB'); d1.write('codeA', 'Fiona secret'); d2.write('codeB', 'George secret'); return (d1.read('codeA') === 'Fiona secret' && d2.read('codeB') === 'George secret' && d1.read('codeB') === 'Access denied') ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Encapsulated state not maintained independently per instance' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }
tests.successMessage: Encapsulation preserves private state across instances ✓
